name: Tool approval
purpose: Require explicit human consent before an agent runs a consequential or external operation.
description: Surfaces what the agent wants to do, the consequence, the affected scope, and explicit approve or reject actions.

good: A destructive external action shows a tool-approval card before the agent proceeds.
bad: A low-risk local read blocks the user behind a tool-approval card.
boundary: A consequential but reversible action may use inline confirmation instead of tool approval.

question.description: What the agent intends to do.

hint.description: Small print under the request. Empty by default.

approve.description: The person approved the request. This is consent to ask for, not authorisation: the host still checks scope and policy before running anything.

reject.description: The person declined. Do not run the tool.

props.title: Run the billing migration?
props.question: Apply three schema changes to the billing database in production.

guidance.summary: Asks a person for explicit consent before an agent or a system runs something consequential.
useWhen: An action is hard to undo, external, or costly, and a person must authorize it.
The scope of the action, such as which data or environment, must be read before deciding.

avoidWhen.text: A low-risk, reversible action: a button is enough.
Work to review, not an operation to authorize.
A form whose submission is the decision: mark the section consequential.

states.label: Idle
states.description: The request is described; nothing is asked yet.

states.label: Pending
states.description: Both decisions are available, with the scope in view.

states.label: Approved
states.description: The host re-renders with the outcome after the person approved.

states.label: Rejected
states.description: The host re-renders with the outcome after the person declined.

states.label: Expired
states.description: The request timed out; the agent must ask again.
states.how: The host re-renders after a timeout.

states.label: Blocked
states.description: Policy forbids the action; it cannot be approved here.
states.how: The host re-renders with the reason.

dos.title: Name exactly what will happen
dos.description: Save 3 corrections to the household record, not Continue.

dos.title: Consequences beside it
dos.description: People approve what they can see changing.

dos.title: The last thing in its part
dos.description: Evidence first, then the decision it informs.

donts.title: Two approvals in one part
donts.description: Neither leads, and people approve the wrong one.

donts.title: Approval as authorization
donts.description: The host checks scope and consent; the click is a request.

content: The question is one sentence; the scope names the data and the environment.

notes: A region named by its title; the outcome is announced politely.
Focus is not trapped: people can read the evidence before deciding.

composition.defaultVisible: The question, the scope, and both decisions.
composition.contentLength: A question under 120 characters; a scope under 90.

redundantWith.reason: A banner announcing that approval is needed.

mistakes: A decision above the evidence that informs it.
Approve labels that do not say what runs.
An approval with no consequences in view.
composition.responsive: Decisions stack full width on a narrow screen.
